decision_reason: Sen2Chain is IRD Espace-DEV's installable Sentinel-2 image-processing package, with a GPL-3.0-or-later grant and full user documentation. KHEOBS's live Sen2Extract service identifies Sen2Chain as the backend used to generate and serve indices, and an IRD-hosted 2025 study reports processing indicators with the Sen2Chain framework. The assigned IRD Forge repo and the documentation-linked Framagit repo have the same current master commit (c47a83d8a42d1eb7f4ed79f29fe7d86661b5fcae), so this is one project, not two products.

government_provenance.note: The GEO Knowledge Hub's exact software record names Sen2Chain and lists IRD, Espace DEV, and Université de La Réunion. IRD is a French public scientific and technological institution (https://en.ird.fr/ird-overview-and-history); the repository's authors include IRD staff and the documentation identifies IRD/University of Reunion development.

public_source.note: The assigned public IRD Forge repository contains the Python package, tests, examples, docs, a GPL licence file, and install metadata. Its current master head exactly matches the Framagit repository that Sen2Chain's own user documentation identifies as the install source.

eligible_license.note: The repository includes the complete GPLv3 text; README.rst says GPLv3+ and pyproject.toml explicitly declares GPL-3.0-or-later and the OSI-approved classifier. The project grant covers Sen2Chain-authored source; dependencies and ESA Sen2Cor retain their separate terms.

primary_evidence.note: The live KHEOBS application says its time-series indices are calculated using Sen2Chain and links the canonical Framagit source; it describes the maintained Sentinel-2 processing/archive workflow. An IRD-hosted 2025 Malaria Journal paper independently reports indicators processed with the Sen2Chain framework: https://horizon.documentation.ird.fr/exl-doc/pleins_textes/2025-03/010092704.pdf.

product_identity: Sen2Chain (Python Sentinel-2 download, correction, cloud-mask, index, and time-series processing package)
agency: Institut de Recherche pour le Développement (IRD), Espace-DEV; developed with Université de La Réunion and research partners
geography: France; used in international research workflows including Cambodia
license: GPL-3.0-or-later for Sen2Chain-authored code; dependencies and ESA Sen2Cor retain their own terms
family_note: The assigned forge.ird.fr repo is an identical current-head copy of the Framagit source linked by first-party documentation. Treat them as one source/product. Sen2Extract is a separate web interface/service that consumes Sen2Chain; its code and license are outside this review.
status_note: The Framagit public repository was created 2019-06-22; although its imported initial commit and GPL file have 2018 timestamps, that predates evidence the code was publicly available, so 2019 is the conservative first public-source year. The project is currently maintained (master activity 2026-09-22); docs describe v1.04.01. No formal GitLab release objects were listed, but documented real scientific use and the live deployment satisfy the notability path.

decision_reason: This public repository is an installable Quarto letter-template extension with GPL-3.0-or-later source and clear setup instructions. Hold because no versioned release, external adoption, or official operational use of this specific extension was found; without that evidence it does not yet meet the agency-published reusable-product notability path. Clear with a versioned release plus user/install guidance or documented independent adoption.

government_provenance.note: The exact project is published under the MARBEC/OB7 namespace on IRD's Forge; IRD's official lab directory confirms MARBEC is a joint research unit under IRD, Ifremer, University of Montpellier, and CNRS. README names this repo as the OB7 Quarto letter extension.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the Quarto extension files, letter template, README, and installation commands for new or existing Quarto projects.

eligible_license.note: The inspected root LICENSE is the full GNU GPL version 3 text, and GitLab identifies the project as GPL-3.0-or-later. No conflicting material-code notice was found.

primary_evidence.note: The README documents how to install the extension, but I found no versioned release/tag, agency deployment, or independent user/adoption record for this exact letter template.

status_note: GitLab project was created publicly on 2024-03-14 with a GPL grant and functional template files; the imported LICENSE commit is dated 2023-02-07, which predates public availability and is not used to backdate the source year. No tags/releases were listed.

decision_reason: This repository is a static bioinformatics help/contact and availability webpage for one MIVEGEC staff member, based on the Start Bootstrap Creative theme; it is not a scheduling application or reusable government software product. The live page presents staff contact and meeting information, not an operational scheduling tool.

government_provenance.note: The official IRD directory confirms MIVEGEC is a public joint research unit. The live page and README identify Jacques Dainat as the MIVEGEC bioinformatics contact; the repository is under the unit's IRD Forge namespace.

public_source.note: The public repository contains HTML/CSS/JavaScript for a static website.

eligible_license.note: The only inspected MIT notice names Blackrock Digital LLC and accompanies the Start Bootstrap theme. I found no separate notice establishing the exact license scope of MIVEGEC's modifications or page content; in any event this is not an eligible software product.

primary_evidence.note: The deployed page provides bioinformatics assistance/contact details and meeting-time information. It is a static informational page, not a software calendar or self-service scheduling tool.
